deposits.notes: One publicly accessible study consent PDF, two pages, fetched and read in memory. Discovery chain: the title search found the c026 arXiv record; https://arxiv.org/src/2409.11360 (HTTP 200) contains 3_methodology.tex, line 44, with the commented-out footnote %\footnote{The portal can be accessed at \url{https://caai-portal.vercel.app}}. This URL is absent from the compiled PDF. The portal returned HTTP 200, and its publicly linked application bundle /_next/static/chunks/app/page-8cea44ef6b9c8b1b.js returned HTTP 200 (6616 bytes) and linked /consent-form.pdf. The consent identifies Dhruv Agarwal, the India/US recruitment restriction, and AI-assisted versus unassisted tasks, corroborating its association with S1. It contains no participant records, actual assignments, outcome scores, or participant texts. Page 1, Privacy and Confidentiality, says: "Your task responses will not be used as data to train any model. They will only be used by the research team for analysis." It also says some demographic details may be reported in aggregate. This is a materials finding, not a promise of data access. The public frontend says participation must begin through Prolific; no consent was submitted, participant session started, account used, or database queried. n_files=1 covers this linked consent PDF, not a claimed exhaustive inventory of website assets. No reuse license was stated in the consent PDF.

notes:
Checked on 2026-10-09 using Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without credentials or personal identifiers. The complete 119022-character markdown was read in consecutive chunks, including references and Appendices A-C; relevant wording and locators were checked against PDF text, and external PDF hyperlinks were enumerated. The local file is arXiv 2409.11360v3, 12 March 2025, 21 pages; the public arXiv landing page (HTTP 200) also identifies v3 as the latest revision. The form contains only S1, and both data_and_code URLs are empty. No data-availability, on-request, preregistration, study-code-release, or external supplementary-file statement was found. Statements above include material locations and data-storage descriptions, which do not assert public data availability.

Public materials consist of the consent document found through the archived source; no public participant-level or output-level dataset was located. The manuscript describes 118 analyzed participants and 472 essays, but no rows or columns from those records could be inspected. Therefore the public material cannot supply per-person means, SDs, SEs, participant-clustered uncertainty for similarity/classifier outcomes, assignment/attrition counts by arm, or the underlying choices needed to resolve the Table 7 discrepancy in final.open_items. The selected essays in Tables 5 and 8 have no participant identifiers and are not a complete sample. Table 7 is an aggregate table, not participant data.

The arXiv source archive at https://arxiv.org/src/2409.11360 returned HTTP 200; its 1100640 bytes were inspected in memory. All 51 file names were enumerated: manuscript/table TeX, bibliography/style files, and PDF/PNG illustrations/plots. No CSV, spreadsheet, participant JSON, analysis notebook, experiment-analysis script, or ancillary raw-data file was present. This article-source archive is not counted as a separate data deposit.

Other checked links: https://languagetool.org/ returned HTTP 200; https://github.com/jxmorris12/language_tool_python returned HTTP 200, and its named GitHub recursive-tree API https://api.github.com/repos/jxmorris12/language_tool_python/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1 returned HTTP 200 with truncated=false. The tree contains the generic grammar-checking package, documentation, examples, and tests, not this experiment’s data or analysis code, so it is excluded from deposits. The OSF DOI in reference [86], https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/mhjn6, returned HTTP 200 after redirecting to https://osf.io/mhjn6. https://api.osf.io/v2/preprints/mhjn6/ returned HTTP 200 and identifies a different paper, Biased AI Writing Assistants Shift Users’ Attitudes on Societal Issues. The corresponding nodes/mhjn6/files/osfstorage/ and nodes/mhjn6/children/ requests returned HTTP 404; the identifier is a preprint, not a c026 data node. This reference is excluded from deposits.

https://doi.org/10.1145/3706598.3713564 redirected to https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3706598.3713564, which returned HTTP 403 with a Just a moment bot-check page. No attempt was made to bypass it. Publisher supplementary files and differences in the ACM version could not be checked. This limitation, and the title-only scope of the specified OSF nodes search, support medium confidence. The conclusion is that only public study materials were confirmed in the checked sources, not that participant data can never be obtained.
